title: The currency in your fund
topic: Exchange rates change what you own

steps.title: One fund, many currencies
steps.body: You buy $1,000 of a fund when €1 is worth $1.25. You pay €800. Then the euro becomes weaker. The fund's price did not change, but now it is worth €1,000. A world fund buys companies in many countries, with prices in dollars, yen or pounds. When the exchange rate changes, the fund's value in euros changes too. This is called [[currency-risk]]. It can make you gain or lose.

steps.prompt: You buy $1,000 of a fund. At that time, €1 is worth $1.00, so you pay €1,000. The fund's price in dollars stays the same. Later, €1 is worth $1.25. How much has your fund gained or lost in euros?
steps.reveal: It lost 20%. Your $1,000 is now worth €800. The share prices did not change. The euro became stronger, so each dollar buys fewer euros.

steps.prompt: True or false: a fund can lose value in euros even if its price in dollars does not change.
steps.explanation: True. When the euro becomes stronger, each dollar is worth fewer euros. This is [[currency-risk]].

steps.prompt: Match each term from this path with its meaning.
pairs: Exchange rates change what your investments are worth in euros
Investing mostly in your own country
The time until you need the money
A fall from a previous high

steps.prompt: The euro becomes 20% stronger against the dollar. The price of a dollar fund stays the same. What happens to its value in euros?
options: Nothing, because the fund's price did not change
steps.explanation: Each dollar now buys fewer euros. So the fund is worth less in euros, even though its dollar price did not move. Exchange rates can help you or hurt you.

steps.title: Your money in other currencies
steps.body: **{worldShare}** of your investment account is in world funds. Most companies in these funds have prices in other currencies. When the euro goes up or down, the value of these funds in euros changes.

steps.prompt: About {worldShare} of your investment account is in other currencies. Move the euro slider. The result shows how your account changes in euros, even if no share price moves.

euroMove.label: Change of the euro against other currencies

output.label: Change of your account in euros

goal.hint: Move a slider to see the result change.

steps.note: The second slider starts at your real share. This is an example. Real funds hold many currencies.

scenes.title: Same fund, new price
scenes.desc: A fund's price in dollars can stay the same while its value in euros changes.

captions.text: You buy $1,000 of a fund when €1 is worth $1.25.
You pay €800. Then the euro becomes weaker.
The fund's price did not change, but now it is worth €1,000.
